en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a perfectly symmetrical stratovolcano cone shape that is easily observable from the surrounding plains of Legazpi City.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable cave where visitors can observe towering limestone stalactites hanging from the ceiling.
The Rafflesia consanguinea flower found in the forests of Bukidnon can grow up to one meter wide and emits a rotting meat smell.
During the dry season, the grass covering the 1,268 cone-shaped mounds of the Chocolate Hills in Bohol turns brown.
Whale sharks migrate to the coastal waters of Donsol in Sorsogon, where observers can see their distinct pattern of white spots and stripes.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds the Main Crater Lake, creating a unique lake-within-a-lake observable feature.
During the amihan season, the Philippines experiences cool northeast monsoon winds that bring dry and cold weather to most parts of the country.
Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental features a unique pygmy forest where century-old bonsai trees grow only a few meters tall due to ultramafic soil.
The twin cascades of Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City plunge roughly 320 feet, creating a massive, observable mist that permanently surrounds the rocks.
Sta. Cruz Island in Zamboanga City gets its distinct pink sand color from the crushed red organ pipe corals mixed with white sand.
The Sumaguing Cave in Sagada contains large limestone stalactites and stalagmites formed over thousands of years by the slow dripping of mineral-rich water.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain, allowing it to see clearly in the dark.
